title: observability: add per-token KV logging, refine dashboards, and tune alerts
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: improve visibility into token-level KV cache behavior and its cost/latency impact. Production incidents showed KV cache miss spikes correlated with a recent model rollout; this PR adds structured per-token KV logging, dashboard improvements for token-level cost/latency breakdowns, and alert tuning to reduce noise while catching regressions.

What this PR does:
- Implements a lightweight, opt-in per-token KV logger that emits structured events for cache hits/misses, size, and latency. Events are sampled by default and include request_id, model, seq_len, and token_index.
- Adds aggregation pipelines and derived metrics for token-level cache hit rate, avg token latency, and per-token cost contributions.
- Ships new Grafana dashboards: Token KV Overview, Token Cost/LAT Breakdown, and KV Health Summary. Dashboards include drilldowns and recommended filters for heavy-hitter tenants.
- Adjusts alert thresholds and grouping to reduce pager noise: move noisy anomaly alerts to warning, introduce composite alerts that require both increased error rate and token latency degradations, and add per-customer noise suppression for noisy test tenants.
- Backwards-compatible additions: logger is disabled by default via config flag (observability.kv_token_logging.enabled=false).

Checklist:
- [x] Add per-token KV logging implementation (server-side, lightweight serializer)
- [x] Add ingestion and aggregation rules in observability pipelines
- [x] Create Grafana dashboards and panel templates
- [x] Update alert rules and runbook (ops/alerts/kv_token_runbook.md)
- [x] Add unit and integration tests for logger and pipelines
- [x] Gradual rollout plan documented in PR description and runbook

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests + integration tests added and run in CI.
- Canary rollout: enable per-token logging for 2% of requests in staging; collect metrics for 48h and validate storage/cost.
- Gradually increase sampling and enable for Dedicated customers on request.
- Rollback: flip config flag to false; aggregation rules are additive and safe to remove.

Notes/links: Linear: ENG-6789. Support ticket: SUP-1123. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/ops/runbooks/kv_token_runbook.md

Impact: improves ability to triage regressions from model rollouts and routing changes, provides token-level cost visibility to SRE and platform teams, and reduces alert fatigue by tuning noisy signals.

summary: Per-token KV cache logging, aggregation pipelines, dashboards, and alert tuning to improve triage and reduce pager noise. Opt-in and sampling controls ensure minimal cost impact.
